claims.text: Premelting and melting behavior in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles is predominantly governed by the surface-energy contribution associated with particle surface-to-volume ratio.
Smaller CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles have a higher surface-energy contribution than larger particles because of their greater surface-to-volume ratio.
Smaller CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles exhibit an earlier onset of premelting than larger particles.
Particle size alters the melting kinetics of CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Changing surface-to-volume ratio modulates the effective surface-energy contribution.
The effective surface-energy contribution affects the stability of surface atoms and drives premelting.
The larger surface-to-volume ratio of smaller nanoparticles increases atomic disorder at their surfaces.
Smaller nanoparticles have reduced cohesive energy at the surface relative to larger particles.
Reduced surface cohesive energy initiates premelting at lower temperatures.
Relative to 20 nm particles, 5 nm CoCrFeMnNi particles will have a lower premelting-onset temperature.
Relative to 20 nm particles, 5 nm CoCrFeMnNi particles will have a broader premelting-temperature range.
Relative to 20 nm particles, 5 nm CoCrFeMnNi particles will display modified melting kinetics.
The proposed size-dependent mechanism should hold approximately over the 5–20 nm particle-size range.
Outside the 5–20 nm range, quantum-size effects or substantial agglomeration may additionally influence melting behavior.
Particle shape and agglomeration are potential confounders of the proposed relationship between size and premelting behavior.
Comparing composition-matched 5 nm, 10 nm, and 20 nm particles under the same inert-atmosphere heating conditions is intended to isolate particle size as the intervention.
